description: Controlled vocabulary for Life Situation Tags v1 (Bible PAL). Maps real-life events to scripture-grounded story retrieval anchors. METADATA-ONLY in v1: not consumed by app routing, not parsed by Parable model. Read by scripts/query_life_situation_tags.py and validated by test/services/life_situation_tag_compliance_test.dart.

tags.description: A close family bond has fractured — through running away, exile, betrayal, or silence. The pain is specifically familial, not romantic or social.
A family member did something cruel or treacherous — sold you out, lied, abandoned. Distinct from general estrangement because there is a specific wrongdoer.
Returning, often humbled, to a place or people you left. The motion is inward and reconciling, not a triumphal arrival.
I am the one extending forgiveness to someone who hurt me — and it costs something. The narrative angle is from the wounded party choosing release.
I am the one who failed, and someone — God, a parent, a friend — has welcomed me back without making me earn it.
Staying with someone through their grief or ruin when leaving would be easier. The loyalty is the story, not the loss itself.
Widowhood — the specific grief of losing a husband or wife. Includes the practical and identity disruption that follows.
Choosing kindness toward people who harmed or opposed you — including people you might rightfully condemn. Distinct from general forgiveness because the recipient is genuinely hostile.
I failed someone who trusted me — broke a promise, lost something entrusted to me, or wasn't there when needed. The shame is relational, not anonymous.
I failed in a way that is hard to face. Not just a mistake — a moral or character failure that I have to live with. The grief is self-directed.
After failing or refusing, I'm being given another opportunity — not because I earned it, but because someone is patient. The story emphasizes the do-over, not the original fall.
Something that was lost — relationship, dignity, possession, health — is being returned. Specifically a return-to-state, not a brand-new beginning.
I have wanted something for a long time — a child, a calling, healing — and it hasn't come. The story sits inside the unfulfilled wait, not the answer.
Something was promised — explicitly or implicitly — and the fulfillment is taking far longer than expected. The faith struggle is the gap itself.

I helped someone and they forgot me. Or I'm in a hard place and the people who could remember me have moved on. Distinct from delayed_promise because the felt wound is being forgotten, not just delay.
Praying through deep grief, dread, or desperation — not composed, not eloquent. The body is in it.
Waiting that took most of a life — and was honored at the end. The story rewards endurance over decades, not weeks.
I know what I'm supposed to do and I'm going the other direction. Active avoidance, not passive reluctance.
I'll do it, but I don't want to and I'm not pretending otherwise. The story includes the unwillingness as part of the obedience.
Yielding to a path I didn't choose — saying "let it be" or "not my will." Broader than surrender_what_you_love; this is the posture, not the specific object given up.
Being asked to give up something specific and precious — a child, a future, a possession. The cost has a name.
Being chosen for something significant when you're young, hidden, or unlikely. The call comes in private, before anyone else knows.
Being asked to do something I don't feel equipped for — by background, skill, or status. The self-doubt is specific and named.
Depleted to the point of wanting to quit or disappear. Not a hard week — a fundamental wearing-out that requires rest and food, not pep talks.
Being harmed for doing the right thing, or for who I am, by someone with power. Includes social, legal, or violent harm.
Locked up or confined when I didn't deserve it — literal or institutional captivity rather than general persecution.
Standing firm without drama — keeping a habit, telling the truth once, refusing once. The courage is shown by what you don't do (cave, lie, flee).
Speaking or living a truth that costs you something serious — your safety, your community, your life.
A decision point where doing right has real consequences and there is no safe option. The story turns on the moment of choosing.
Confronting a ruler, authority, or institution with what they don't want to hear. Risk is asymmetric — they hold the power.
Living with sickness — chronic, sudden, or shameful. Includes the disability and the social weight that comes with it.
Healing required setting aside pride or prestige — accepting help on someone else's terms. The pride is the obstacle, not the disease.
A storm — literal or otherwise — arrives without warning and overwhelms. The story sits inside the surprise, not the aftermath.
Fear that takes over the body — sleeplessness, panic, paralysis. Not anxiety as a mood but fear as a flood.
The crisis hasn't ended, but someone is *with me* inside it. The comfort is companionship in the danger, not removal of the danger.
I started well and then fear pulled me under mid-action — losing nerve in the middle of obedience. Specifically about momentum lost partway.
Belief that flickers — not lost, not solid. Doubt that coexists with continued reaching.
Something about my history or current life that I work to keep hidden. The story turns on being known anyway.
Kindness arriving where I expected judgment or being passed over. The surprise is the kindness, not the situation that prompted it.
Encountered by someone who knows the truth about me without my telling them — and stays. The relief is being fully visible without being rejected.
Something irreplaceable went missing — a possession, a person, an opportunity. The story sits inside the loss itself.
Active, diligent pursuit of what is lost — sweeping the house, walking the hills. The labor of looking is the story.
The lost thing — coin, sheep, person — is recovered, and the recovery prompts unreasonable joy. The story ends in shared celebration.
Needs being met through small, often unnoticed channels — extra grain, a daily jar, a stranger's kindness. Distinct from miraculous rescue.
Beginning again in a new place or season after loss — with little, but moving forward. The story is the first steps of the new chapter, not the catastrophe behind.
